title: Social Justice & Empowerment: Schemes, Acts, Policies

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 17 of the Constitution defines the term 'untouchability' and prescribes the punishment for it.
2. The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 was originally enacted as the Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955.
3. Article 35 empowers Parliament alone, and not State Legislatures, to make laws prescribing punishment for the practice of untouchability.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 17 only abolishes untouchability and forbids it in any form; the Constitution never defines the word. The 1955 Act was renamed in 1976 and, under Article 35, only Parliament can prescribe punishment for Article 17 offences so that the penalty is uniform across States.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Indian Polity Ch Fundamental Rights (Right to Equality); Art 35
questions.h: Art 17 abolishes, Art 35 punishes: only Parliament holds the stick.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989:
1. The 2015 amendment added new offences and provided for Exclusive Special Courts for speedy trial.
2. Section 18A, inserted in 2018, removes the need for a preliminary enquiry before registering an FIR and bars anticipatory bail.
3. In Subhash Kashinath Mahajan (2018), the Supreme Court had laid down a preliminary enquiry and prior approval before arrest.
4. In Prathvi Raj Chauhan (2020), the Supreme Court struck down Section 18A as unconstitutional.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 2018 Mahajan safeguards were seen as diluting the Act, so Parliament inserted Section 18A to restore the original position. In Prathvi Raj Chauhan (2020) the Court upheld Section 18A, though it said courts may still quash a plainly false FIR.
questions.s: PRS / SC judgments; Laxmikanth Ch Fundamental Rights; The Hindu, Feb 2020

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Constitutional provision : Amendment that introduced it
1. Article 15(5) (reservation in educational institutions including private unaided) : 93rd Amendment, 2005
2. Article 16(4A) (reservation in promotions for SC/ST) : 81st Amendment, 2000
3. Article 16(4B) (carry forward of unfilled vacancies) : 81st Amendment, 2000
4. Article 15(6) (reservation for economically weaker sections) : 104th Amendment, 2019
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Article 16(4A) came through the 77th Amendment (1995) to undo the effect of Indra Sawhney on promotions; the 81st Amendment added 16(4B). The EWS clause 15(6) came through the 103rd Amendment, not the 104th (which extended SC/ST seat reservation in legislatures).
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Indian Polity Ch Fundamental Rights; list of Constitutional Amendments

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT laid down by the Supreme Court in Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992)?
o: Backward classes under Article 16(4) cannot be identified on the basis of economic criteria alone.
The 'creamy layer' among the Other Backward Classes must be excluded from the benefit of reservation.
Reservation under Article 16(4) can be extended to promotions as a permanent feature of the Constitution.
The total reservation under Article 16(4) should ordinarily not exceed 50 per cent.
questions.e: The Court held that Article 16(4) does not extend to promotions (allowing only a five-year grace period); Parliament then inserted Article 16(4A) through the 77th Amendment (1995). The other three were all part of the judgment.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Indian Polity Ch Fundamental Rights; Indra Sawhney (1992)
questions.h: Promotion ban in 1992, Art 16(4A) fix in 1995.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) reservation:
1. The 103rd Constitutional Amendment inserted Articles 15(6) and 16(6) to enable reservation for economically weaker sections.
2. The EWS quota is meant for sections other than those already covered by the reservation for SCs, STs and socially and educationally backward classes.
3. In Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (2022), the Supreme Court struck down the amendment as violating the basic structure.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The amendment (in force 2019) created a separate 10 per cent category for the economically weaker among unreserved groups. A five-judge Bench upheld it by a 3:2 majority in November 2022, so the third statement is wrong.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Indian Polity Ch Fundamental Rights; Janhit Abhiyan (2022)

questions.q:
Match List-I (Constitutional Article) with List-II (Subject):
A. Article 338
B. Article 338A
C. Article 338B
D. Article 342A
1. National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
2. National Commission for Backward Classes
3. National Commission for Scheduled Castes
4. Specification of socially and educationally backward classes by the President
questions.e: Article 338 (SC) was split by the 89th Amendment (2003) to create 338A (ST); the 102nd Amendment (2018) gave constitutional status to the backward classes commission under 338B and inserted 342A on the SEBC list.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Indian Polity Ch National Commissions for SC, ST and BC
questions.h: 338 SC, 338A ST, 338B BC: the letters follow the order the bodies were created.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: A Presidential notification specifying the Scheduled Castes of a State cannot be varied by a later executive notification.
Statement-II: Article 341(2) vests in Parliament, by law, the power to include or exclude any caste from the list issued under Article 341(1).
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Article 341(1) lets the President, after consulting the Governor, specify the castes; clause (2) then freezes the list against executive tinkering and makes Parliament the only body that can amend it. This keeps the schedule uniform and stops State-level politics from altering it.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Indian Polity Ch Special Provisions for SC/ST; Art 341

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 102nd and 105th Constitutional Amendments:
1. The 102nd Amendment (2018) inserted Articles 338B and 342A in the Constitution.
2. After the 105th Amendment (2021), only the President can specify the list of socially and educationally backward classes, and States have no role.
3. Under Article 342A(1), the President specifies the socially and educationally backward classes of a State after consulting the Governor.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Supreme Court's 2021 Maratha quota ruling read Article 342A as giving the President exclusive power, which took away State lists. The 105th Amendment reversed that by allowing States and Union Territories to prepare their own SEBC lists, so the second statement is wrong.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Indian Polity Ch National Commission for Backward Classes; Jayashri Patil (2021)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Mandal Commission:
1. It was appointed in 1979 under Article 340 of the Constitution.
2. It recommended 27 per cent reservation for Other Backward Classes in services and educational institutions.
3. The Government announced the implementation of its recommendation for central services in August 1990.
4. It was the first Backward Classes Commission of independent India.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Kalelkar Commission (1953) was the first backward classes commission; Mandal (set up 1979, report 1980) was the second. The 27 per cent figure was added to the 22.5 per cent for SC/ST, keeping the total just under the 50 per cent ceiling.
questions.s: Spectrum / Laxmikanth Ch Fundamental Rights; PIB
questions.h: Mandal 1979-80, 27 per cent, and the 1990 order: 79, 27, 90.

questions.q: The commission headed by Justice G. Rohini, constituted in 2017 under Article 340, was mandated to
o: revise the creamy-layer ceiling applicable to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
identify economically weaker sections among the unreserved communities.
recommend the inclusion of Dalit converts to Christianity and Islam in the Scheduled Castes list.
examine the sub-categorisation of castes within the Other Backward Classes in the Central List.
questions.e: The Rohini Commission looked at unequal sharing of the 27 per cent OBC quota among castes and submitted its report in July 2023. The question of SC status for Dalit converts is the subject of a separate commission headed by Justice K. G. Balakrishnan (2022).
questions.s: PIB, 2017 / The Hindu, Aug 2023

questions.q: Based on the present delimitation, the number of seats reserved in the Lok Sabha for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes is, respectively,
questions.e: After the 2008 Delimitation Act, 84 SC and 47 ST seats are reserved out of 543. The older figures, 79 and 41, belong to the pre-2008 arrangement.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Indian Polity Ch Parliament / Special Provisions; Art 330

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 104th Constitutional Amendment:
1. It extended the reservation of seats for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies up to 2030.
2. It continued the nomination of Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies for ten more years.
3. Under Article 330 as it stands, the seats reserved for SCs in a State's Lok Sabha quota are proportional to the SC population share of that State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 104th Amendment (effective January 2020) extended the SC/ST seat reservation by ten years but ended the Anglo-Indian nominations under Articles 331 and 333. Article 330 fixes reserved seats in proportion to each State's SC or ST population.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Indian Polity Ch Special Provisions for Certain Classes

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Supreme Court's 2024 judgment on sub-classification of Scheduled Castes (State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh):
1. A seven-judge Bench held, by a 6:1 majority, that States can sub-classify Scheduled Castes for the purpose of reservation.
2. The judgment overruled the earlier decision in E. V. Chinnaiah v. State of Andhra Pradesh (2004).
3. The Court held that sub-classification must rest on quantifiable and demonstrable data on inadequate representation and not on whim or political expediency.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Court reasoned that Scheduled Castes are not a homogeneous group, so more backward castes within the list can be given a share of the quota. States must back this with empirical data, which is a safeguard against arbitrary or political sub-quotas.
questions.s: The Hindu / Supreme Court, 1 Aug 2024
questions.h: Seven judges, six to one: sub-classification allowed, data required.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Scheduled Castes list:
1. The Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950 originally recognised only Hindus as members of the Scheduled Castes.
2. Sikhs were included in the list by the 1950 Order itself.
3. Buddhists were brought into the list through an amendment in 1990.
4. Under the Order as it stands, a person professing Christianity or Islam is not deemed to be a member of a Scheduled Caste.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 1950 Order tied the status to the Hindu religion on the reasoning that untouchability was a Hindu social practice. Sikhs were added in 1956 and Buddhists in 1990, but Christians and Muslims remain outside, so the second statement is the wrong one.
questions.s: Spectrum / Ministry of Social Justice; Laxmikanth Ch Special Provisions

questions.q: Which one of the following Articles empowers the President to appoint a commission to investigate the conditions of socially and educationally backward classes?
questions.e: Article 340 is the source of the Kalelkar, Mandal and Rohini commissions. Article 338B creates the standing National Commission for Backward Classes, 342A deals with the list of backward classes and Article 46 is a Directive Principle.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Indian Polity Ch Special Provisions for Certain Classes; Art 340

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Fifth and Sixth Schedules:
1. The Fifth Schedule applies to the administration of tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
2. The Sixth Schedule provides for Autonomous District Councils in the tribal areas it covers.
3. The Fifth Schedule provides for a Tribes Advisory Council in each State having Scheduled Areas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Sixth Schedule (Article 244(2)) covers the four North-Eastern States and gives self-rule through district councils; the Fifth Schedule (Article 244(1)) covers Scheduled Areas in the remaining States. The first statement swaps the two.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Indian Polity Ch Scheduled and Tribal Areas

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about tribal rights legislation:
1. The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 extends Part IX of the Constitution to Fifth Schedule areas with modifications.
2. The Bhuria Committee recommendations led to the enactment of the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act.
3. The Forest Rights Act, 2006 recognises forest rights only of Scheduled Tribes and excludes other traditional forest dwellers.
4. Under the Forest Rights Act, the Gram Sabha initiates the process of determining the nature and extent of individual and community forest rights.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The FRA 2006 covers both Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers, so the third statement is wrong. PESA 1996 followed the Bhuria Committee (1995) and made the Gram Sabha the centre of tribal self-governance.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Indian Polity Ch Panchayati Raj; Ministry of Tribal Affairs

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Eklavya Model Residential Schools are meant for Scheduled Tribe students.
2. The PM-JANMAN mission, launched in November 2023, is intended for all Scheduled Tribe communities.
3. Janjatiya Gaurav Divas is observed on 15 November, the birth anniversary of Birsa Munda.
4. The Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan is a scheme of the Ministry of Rural Development.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: PM-JANMAN targets the Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups, not all tribes, and the Dharti Aaba Abhiyan belongs to the Ministry of Tribal Affairs. Janjatiya Gaurav Divas on 15 November marks Birsa Munda's birth anniversary.
questions.s: PIB, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, 2023-24

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT among the traditional criteria for identifying a community as a Scheduled Tribe?
o: Shyness of contact with the community at large
questions.e: The Constitution does not define a Scheduled Tribe; the practice that grew from the Lokur Committee (1965) uses indications of primitive traits, distinctive culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact and backwardness. Numerical dominance is not a criterion; many tribes are small groups.
questions.s: Ministry of Tribal Affairs; Laxmikanth Ch Special Provisions

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding manual scavenging:
1. The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013 applies only to dry latrines and not to sewers or septic tanks.
2. The 2013 Act was the first Central law to prohibit the employment of manual scavengers.
3. The NAMASTE scheme is implemented jointly by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 2013 Act replaced the 1993 prohibition law and extended the ban to hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks. NAMASTE (National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem) aims to shift sewer and septic tank work to mechanised, protected methods.
questions.s: PIB, MoSJE / MoHUA; Ministry of Social Justice

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 as amended in 2017:
1. Maternity leave is 26 weeks for the first two children.
2. Establishments with 50 or more employees must provide crèche facilities.
3. The 26-week leave applies to the third child as well.
4. After the leave period, the employer may allow a woman to work from home if the nature of work permits and by mutual agreement.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 2017 amendment raised leave from 12 to 26 weeks for the first two children, but for a third child or more the leave remains 12 weeks. The crèche duty applies from 50 employees and work-from-home is an optional arrangement.
questions.s: PIB, 2017; Ministry of Labour and Employment
questions.h: 26 weeks for the first two, 12 for the third: two children, two quarters.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Under the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 as amended in 2005, a daughter is a coparcener by birth in joint Hindu family property even if her father died before 9 September 2005.
Statement-II: The Supreme Court in Vineeta Sharma v. Rakesh Sharma (2020) held that the coparcenary right accrues by birth and does not depend on the father being alive on the date of the amendment.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The 2005 amendment gave daughters the same coparcenary rights as sons, but courts earlier differed on whether the father had to be alive on the cut-off date. Vineeta Sharma settled it: the right comes by birth, so the cut-off date does not matter.
questions.s: The Hindu, Aug 2020; Supreme Court

questions.q: Mission Shakti, the integrated scheme for women's safety, security and empowerment, has two sub-schemes. They are
questions.e: Sambal covers safety and security (One Stop Centres, Women Helpline, Beti Bachao Beti Padhao) while Samarthya covers empowerment (Shakti Sadan, Sakhi Niwas, crèches and maternity benefit). Both come under the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
questions.s: PIB, Ministry of Women and Child Development

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023 (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam), as originally enacted:
1. It reserves one-third of seats in the Rajya Sabha and State Legislative Councils for women.
2. One-third of the seats reserved for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies are to be reserved for women of those groups.
3. The reservation was to take effect only after a delimitation exercise undertaken following the first Census after the Act came into force.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Act covers the Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies and the Delhi Assembly, not the Rajya Sabha or Legislative Councils. Its delimitation condition made the start date depend on the Census, which is why implementation has been debated.
questions.s: PRS Legislative Research / PIB, Sep 2023; Drishti IAS, Apr 2026

questions.q: Under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Act, 2021, the upper gestational limit for termination for special categories such as survivors of rape is
questions.e: The 2021 amendment raised the limit from 20 to 24 weeks for special categories, and removed any limit when a Medical Board finds substantial foetal abnormalities. The general limit for other women remains 20 weeks, which is the tempting wrong option.
questions.s: PRS Legislative Research; MoHFW
questions.h: 20 to 24: the Act added four weeks.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005:
1. A woman in a relationship in the nature of marriage can seek protection under the Act.
2. The Act recognises the right of the aggrieved woman to reside in the shared household.
3. Protection Officers under the Act are appointed by the Central Government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Act covers live-in relationships and secures the right to residence in the shared household, whatever the title to the property. Protection Officers are appointed by the State Government, not the Centre.
questions.s: Ministry of Women and Child Development; Laxmikanth Ch Fundamental Rights

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013:
1. An Internal Committee is required only in workplaces with 50 or more employees.
2. A Local Committee is constituted at the district level to handle complaints from establishments that have no Internal Committee.
3. The Act was enacted after the Supreme Court laid down guidelines in Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan (1997).
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Internal Committee is required at every office or branch with ten or more employees, not fifty. The 2013 Act converted the Vishaka guidelines into a statute.
questions.s: PRS; Laxmikanth Ch Fundamental Rights

questions.q:
Match List-I (Legislation concerning women) with List-II (Year of enactment):
A. Dowry Prohibition Act
B. Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act
C. Indecent Representation of Women (Prohibition) Act
D. Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act
1. 1956
2. 1961
3. 1986
4. 2005
questions.e: The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act dates from 1956 (originally the Suppression of Immoral Traffic Act), the Dowry Prohibition Act from 1961 and the Indecent Representation Act from 1986. The domestic violence law came in 2005.
questions.s: Ministry of Women and Child Development; India Code

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Commission for Women:
1. It is a statutory body constituted under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990.
2. It has the powers of a criminal court while investigating complaints.
3. Its Chairperson is nominated by the Central Government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The NCW (constituted in 1992 under the 1990 Act) is a statutory, not constitutional, body. While investigating, it has the powers of a civil court, not a criminal court, and its Chairperson is nominated by the Centre.
questions.s: Ministry of Women and Child Development; NCW Act, 1990

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015:
1. A child aged 16 to 18 years accused of a heinous offence may be tried as an adult after a preliminary assessment by the Juvenile Justice Board.
2. The Central Adoption Resource Authority is a constitutional body under the Act.
3. Child Welfare Committees deal with children in need of care and protection.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 2015 Act was passed after the 2012 Delhi gang-rape case, which led to the provision for a preliminary assessment. CARA is a statutory body, given statutory status by this Act, not a constitutional one.
questions.s: PRS; Ministry of Women and Child Development

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012:
1. The Act is gender-neutral and protects both male and female children.
2. The 2019 amendment introduced death penalty for aggravated penetrative sexual assault.
3. For the purposes of the Act, a 'child' is any person below the age of 16 years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: POCSO defines a child as any person below 18 years and protects boys and girls alike. The 2019 amendment toughened penalties, including capital punishment for aggravated penetrative assault.
questions.s: PRS; Ministry of Women and Child Development

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Right to Education Act, 2009 requires private unaided schools to admit children from economically weaker and disadvantaged groups to at least 25 per cent of the seats at the entry level.
Statement-II: The State reimburses private schools for such children, subject to the lower of the per-child expenditure in State schools and the school's actual fee.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Section 12(1)(c) of the RTE Act reserves 25 per cent of entry-level seats, and Section 12(2) provides reimbursement from the State. The reimbursement is a separate financial arrangement, so it does not explain why the quota exists.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Indian Polity Ch Fundamental Rights; RTE Act 2009

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT done by the Constitution (Eighty-sixth Amendment) Act, 2002?
o: Addition of a Fundamental Duty of parents to provide education opportunities to their children
Substitution of Article 45 on early childhood care and education
Insertion of Article 21A on free and compulsory education for children aged six to fourteen
Insertion of Article 39A on equal justice and free legal aid
questions.e: The 86th Amendment inserted Article 21A, substituted Article 45 (now early childhood care for children under six) and added Article 51A(k). Article 39A was inserted much earlier by the 42nd Amendment (1976).
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Indian Polity Ch Fundamental Rights; Directive Principles

questions.q: Under the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2016, an 'adolescent' is a person who has completed
o: 15 years of age but not yet 18 years
14 years of age but not yet 18 years
12 years of age but not yet 16 years
14 years of age but not yet 16 years
questions.e: The 2016 amendment banned all work for children below 14 (except helping family in non-hazardous work after school) and barred adolescents aged 14 to 18 from hazardous occupations. The 15-to-18 range is the definition used in the Factories Act.
questions.s: PRS; Ministry of Labour and Employment

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a service provided under the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) scheme?
o: Mid-day meals for primary school children
questions.e: ICDS, begun on 2 October 1975, offers six services through Anganwadi Centres: supplementary nutrition, immunisation, health check-ups, referral services, pre-school education and nutrition and health education. Mid-day meals for schoolchildren come under the PM POSHAN scheme of the Ministry of Education.
questions.s: Ministry of Women and Child Development; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR):
1. It is a constitutional body under Article 338.
2. It is a statutory body set up under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005.
3. It functions under the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 338 deals with the Scheduled Castes Commission, not NCPCR. NCPCR was set up in 2007 under the 2005 Act and also monitors the implementation of the Right to Education Act.
questions.s: Ministry of Women and Child Development

questions.q:
Match List-I (Scheme) with List-II (Target group or purpose):
A. PM YASASVI
B. SMILE
C. PM-AJAY
D. NAMASTE
1. Persons engaged in begging and transgender persons
2. Sewer and septic tank workers
3. OBC, EBC and DNT students
4. Socio-economic development of Scheduled Caste communities
questions.e: PM YASASVI is an education scheme for OBC, Economically Backward Class and Denotified Tribe students; SMILE supports livelihood for transgender persons and those engaged in begging; PM-AJAY merged three earlier SC schemes; NAMASTE protects sanitation workers.
questions.s: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment; PIB
questions.h: YASASVI = students, SMILE = smiles for the marginalised.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007:
1. A 'senior citizen' is a citizen of India aged 60 years or above.
2. Parents can claim maintenance under the Act only if they are themselves aged 60 or above.
3. Maintenance Tribunals under the Act are headed by a sitting High Court judge.
4. An appeal against a Maintenance Tribunal order lies to an Appellate Tribunal presided over by an officer of the rank of District Magistrate.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Parents of any age can claim maintenance from their children, while senior citizens without children can claim from relatives who inherit their property. Tribunals are presided over by an officer not below Sub-Divisional Officer rank, not by a High Court judge.
questions.s: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment; PRS

questions.q: Under the Ayushman Vay Vandana scheme extended under AB PM-JAY in October 2024, health cover is provided to
o: citizens aged 60 years and above who are below the poverty line
citizens aged 65 years and above who do not pay income tax
all citizens aged 70 years and above, irrespective of income
all citizens aged 75 years and above, irrespective of income
questions.e: The 2024 extension made every citizen aged 70 or above eligible for a Vay Vandana card, whatever their income. The scheme covers hospitalisation up to Rs 5 lakh per family per year, with senior citizens sharing the top-up.
questions.s: PIB, 29 Oct 2024

questions.q: Which one of the following Directive Principles directs the State to make effective provision for public assistance in cases of old age, sickness and disablement?
questions.e: Article 41 deals with the right to work, education and public assistance in old age, sickness, disablement and undeserved want, within the limits of economic capacity. Article 42 is about just conditions of work and maternity relief, and Article 47 concerns nutrition and public health.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Indian Polity Ch Directive Principles of State Policy

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a component of the National Social Assistance Programme?
o: Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme
Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme
questions.e: NSAP, a Ministry of Rural Development scheme, includes the Indira Gandhi old age, widow and disability pensions and the National Family Benefit Scheme. Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana is the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment's umbrella scheme for senior citizens.
questions.s: Ministry of Rural Development; Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016:
1. The Act recognises 21 specified disabilities.
2. It provides for 3 per cent reservation in government jobs for persons with benchmark disabilities.
3. A 'benchmark disability' means a disability of at least 50 per cent.
4. It provides for a 10 per cent horizontal reservation in higher educational institutions.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Act expanded the 7 disabilities of the 1995 law to 21. It raised the job quota from 3 to 4 per cent, defines benchmark disability as at least 40 per cent, and reserves 5 per cent seats in higher education.
questions.s: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment; PRS

questions.q:
Match List-I (Legislation) with List-II (Year of enactment):
A. Rehabilitation Council of India Act
B. National Trust for Welfare of Persons with Autism, Cerebral Palsy, Mental Retardation and Multiple Disabilities Act
C. Mental Healthcare Act
D. Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act
1. 1992
2. 1995
3. 1999
4. 2017
questions.e: The Rehabilitation Council Act (1992) and the PwD Act (1995) came before the National Trust Act (1999). The 1995 Act was replaced by the 2016 Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, while the Mental Healthcare Act came in 2017.
questions.s: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities; India Code

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Under the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017, a person who attempts suicide is presumed, unless proved otherwise, to be suffering from severe stress and shall not be tried or punished.
Statement-II: The Act empowers a person with mental illness to make an advance directive stating how she wishes, or does not wish, to be treated.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are features of the 2017 Act, which follows a rights-based approach after India ratified the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities. They are independent provisions, so the second does not explain the first.
questions.s: PRS; Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

questions.q:
Match List-I (Commission/Committee) with List-II (Subject):
A. Sachar Committee
B. Dhebar Commission
C. Kaka Kalelkar Commission
D. Ranganath Misra Commission
1. First Backward Classes Commission
2. Religious and linguistic minorities
3. Socio-economic and educational status of Muslims
4. Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes
questions.e: Sachar (2005-06) studied the condition of Muslims, Dhebar (1960) the Scheduled Areas and tribes, and Kalelkar (1953) was the first backward classes commission. Ranganath Misra (2004-07) looked at religious and linguistic minorities.
questions.s: Spectrum; Laxmikanth Ch Special Provisions

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Supreme Court's judgment in NALSA v. Union of India (2014):
1. It recognised transgender persons as a 'third gender'.
2. It directed that transgender persons be treated as Scheduled Castes for the purpose of reservation.
3. It held that a person's gender identity is self-determined and cannot be made conditional on sex reassignment surgery.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Court asked the Centre and States to treat transgender persons as socially and educationally backward classes (OBC), not as Scheduled Castes. It grounded the rights in Articles 14, 15, 16, 19 and 21.
questions.s: The Hindu, Apr 2014; Supreme Court

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about transgender law in India:
1. The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019 allowed recognition through a District Magistrate's certificate based on the applicant's self-perceived gender identity.
2. The amendment passed by Parliament in March 2026 makes certification by a medical board a precondition for recognition by the District Magistrate.
3. The National Council for Transgender Persons under the 2019 Act is chaired by the Union Home Minister.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 2019 Act followed NALSA and allowed self-perceived identity, but the March 2026 amendment shifted to a medical-board route, which critics say departs from NALSA. The National Council is chaired by the Union Minister in charge of Social Justice and Empowerment.
questions.s: Jurist / PRS reports on the Transgender Persons Amendment, Mar 2026

questions.q: Under the SMILE scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, which of the following is the shelter home for transgender persons?
questions.e: SMILE (Support for Marginalised Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise) has sub-schemes for transgender persons and for persons engaged in begging. Garima Greh offers shelter, food and skills to transgender persons, while Swadhar Greh and Ujjawala serve women in difficulty and trafficking victims.
questions.s: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment; PIB

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about minorities in India:
1. Under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992, a 'minority' is a community notified as such by the Central Government.
2. Jains were notified as a national minority community in 2014.
3. The Ministry of Minority Affairs was created in January 2006.
4. Zoroastrians (Parsis) were notified as a minority along with Jains in 2014.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Constitution does not define 'minority'; the NCM Act leaves it to notification. Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists and Zoroastrians were notified in 1993, and Jains were the sixth community added in 2014.
questions.s: Ministry of Minority Affairs; PIB

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: In its interim order of September 2025, the Supreme Court stayed the provision of the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025 that required a person to have practised Islam for five years to create a waqf.
Statement-II: There was no mechanism or rules to determine whether a person had practised Islam for five years.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The Court stayed the clause until the government frames rules to verify religious practice, since without a mechanism it could operate arbitrarily. It also stayed the Collector's power to decide whether waqf property is government land, but did not stay the whole Act.
questions.s: Drishti IAS, 17 Sep 2025
